plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bid half of your value. This is because bidding higher risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing the item to someone who values it more. In this case, my value is $31, so half of that is $15.50. This strategy aims to win only when my valuation exceeds others' enough to justify the cost.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks winning the auction at a loss. Bidding slightly below your value ensures you win only when the potential profit is positive. Since this is round 1, and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value of $22 to maximize potential profit while minimizing risk.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because any bid above your value risks winning at a loss. Bidding too low risks losing to a slightly higher bid and missing out on potential profit. Since it's round 1 and there's no history, I'll bid slightly below my value, anticipating others will do the same. A bid of $39.5 aims to win against conservative bidders while avoiding overpaying.
